body:
**User impact:** when a split is accepted *inside* a running `pdca flow`, the flow now adopts the children itself — but `pdca split --accept` still prints the standalone hint telling the operator to run `pdca flow <child-ids>`. An operator who follows the instruction they were just given starts a second driver over the same bundles while the first is mid-run. There is no per-bundle lock on the drive path, so nothing stops the two runs from stepping on each other's state.

### Root cause

The hint is unconditional: it predates adoption, when restarting the flow by hand was the *only* way to reach the children. Since the adoption core (#472) it is correct **only** when the split was accepted outside a flow.

### Suggested fix — two layers, either useful alone

1. **Make the hint conditional.** Suppress it when `--accept` runs inside a flow that will adopt the children (the drive path already knows it is going to reschedule them); keep it for a standalone `pdca split --accept`.
2. **Add a drive-path lock.** The deeper gap is that two drivers can hold the same bundle at once. A per-bundle lock would fail the second run loudly instead of letting it interleave — worth having independently of the hint, since the same race is reachable by any operator running two flows over overlapping ids.

Surfaced by the pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-08-10 (`process/act-log.md`); §10 candidate of the issue_472 cycle.
title: split --accept prints the "pdca flow <child-ids>" hint even inside a flow that will adopt the children — following it races the run
